page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and memory throughput. The server achieved top-tier results in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions and encryption, alongside a top-tier Geekbench ray tracing score. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests rank in the top 25%, as do memory bandwidth reads and writes. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier. In database operations, the instance demonstrates strong performance, processing 105.14 million Redis SET operations per second.

While the instance excels at memory-bound tasks and parallel processing, it exhibits limitations in large-scale LLM text generation, with the 70B model text generation benchmark falling into the bottom 25%. This highlights a tradeoff where raw CPU-bound inference on massive models is less efficient without dedicated GPU acceleration. Given its high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and 100 Gbps network bandwidth, the x2idn.32xlarge is highly suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise-grade database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
